name: PowerView - Find AS-REP Roastable Accounts
description: Enumerates domain accounts with 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' set (UAC flag UF_DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH=4194304). These accounts are AS-REP roastable — their TGT response is encrypted with their NT hash and can be requested without credentials. Run this before Rubeus asreproast to identify targets.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== WHY ENUMERATE BEFORE ROASTING ===
Blind AS-REP roasting (try every user) creates more Kerberos traffic and noise.
Enumerating vulnerable accounts first lets you:
  1. Understand scope (how many accounts are misconfigured)
  2. Target high-value accounts specifically (service accounts, admins)
  3. Know what you're cracking before you start

=== UAC FLAG: UF_DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH ===
useraccountcontrol value includes 4194304 (0x400000) when pre-auth is disabled.
PowerView's -PreauthNotRequired filter handles this for you — no manual UAC math needed.

=== OUTPUT TO LOOK FOR ===
  samaccountname    userprincipalname          useraccountcontrol
  mmorgan           mmorgan@INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL 4194304
Any account listed here is immediately roastable.

High-value targets to check:
  - Service accounts (svc-*, sqlsvc, etc.) — often have weak passwords
  - Admin-looking accounts — if crackable = direct privilege escalation
  - Regular user accounts — weaker passwords but lower privilege

=== BLOODHOUND ALTERNATIVE ===
BloodHound also shows AS-REP roastable accounts:
  Node: User → Properties → 'AS-REP Roastable: True'
  Pre-built query: 'List all AS-REP Roastable Accounts'

=== CROSS-FOREST ===
AS-REP roasting can work across forest trusts if pre-auth is disabled on
accounts in a trusted forest. Check foreign forests too if trust exists.

=== CHAIN ===
This card (enumerate) → ad-rubeus-asrep (request + crack) → lateral movement

defense.why_it_works: PowerView finds accounts with 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' set (userAccountControl bit) - the AS-REP roasting targets - via LDAP.
defense.impact: The list of AS-REP roastable accounts.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1558.004] LDAP query on userAccountControl for DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH (4662); PowerView in 4104 logs.
defense.artifacts: LDAP UAC query; the no-preauth account list.
defense.prevention: Enable Kerberos pre-authentication (disable only when truly required); enforce 25+ character passwords for any account that must have it off; quarterly review of no-preauth accounts; Defender for Identity detects AS-REP roasting.
defense.evasion: A single scoped LDAP read blends; no 4768 generated at this step.
defense.misconfiguration: The 'Do Not Require Kerberos Preauthentication' checkbox is enabled on the user account (msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes or the UAC flag UF_DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH = 0x400000). This means the KDC issues an AS-REP with the user's session key encrypted by their password hash — without demanding proof of identity first.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Active Directory user account attribute (via ADUC or ADSI Edit)
# 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' = CHECKED
# In PowerShell:
Set-ADAccountControl -Identity svc_backup -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $true

# UAC flag value: 0x400000 (4194304)
# Confirmed with:
Get-ADUser svc_backup -Properties DoesNotRequirePreAuth
defense.secure_config:
# Enforce Kerberos pre-authentication (the secure default)
# In PowerShell:
Set-ADAccountControl -Identity svc_backup -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $false

# Bulk fix — find and fix all no-preauth accounts:
Get-ADUser -Filter {DoesNotRequirePreAuth -eq $true} -Properties DoesNotRequirePreAuth |
  Set-ADAccountControl -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $false

# GPO path (Kerberos policy):
# Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings >
# Account Policies > Kerberos Policy
# 'Maximum lifetime for user ticket' should be set (forces preauth implicitly)

variations.label: Targeted AS-REP (set the UAC flag if you have write)
